Hi all —

Thanks for the redlines, Jill. I reviewed Acme_MSA_redlines_v3 and here are suggested responses we can present on the call. High-level: we can accept a mutual indemnity and move to a $5M cap with carve-outs for gross negligence/fraud; data residency language needs a scoped approach to cover PHI flow and deletion obligations without committing to a multi-year residency guarantee.

Proposed edits (short):
- Section 6: change to mutual indemnification; cap at $5,000,000; add explicit carve-out for willful misconduct and gross negligence.
- Data residency: add clause that customer data designated as PHI will be processed and stored in US regions; Redwood will provide documented deletion process within 30 days of termination for PHI.

Open items for procurement/legal discussion on call:
1) Whether Acme requires contractual certification of our encryption key management (we can offer a KMS/HSM integration note + SOC2 reference).
2) Whether Acme needs a contractual SLA for data deletion timing beyond the 30-day target.

I uploaded a vendor setup checklist for procurement to review and to make sure onboarding tasks are visible: vendor-setup-checklist.xlsx (see attachment).

I can take the lead drafting the redline doc and will circulate a tracked copy within 4 hours of our call.

—Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
